purpose: This artifact describes the schema spine v0 for Rig Relay's Contract-Satisfaction Compiler. It introduces seven new schemas that define canonical JSON/JSONL artifacts for compiler runs, candidates, worktree lifecycle, counterexamples, validation matrix results, permutation corpus rows, and pattern reports. This is schema/data infrastructure only — no compiler runtime, no Python generation, no Jinja2 templates, no worktree creation.

schemas_introduced.purpose: One compiler run manifest: inputs, outputs, budget, slice configuration, artifact paths, and aggregate statistics.
One schema/code candidate record: identification, status, hashes, worktree reference, and optional fit score.
One worktree lifecycle event row: state transitions, kind, dirty state, and cleanup actions.
One compiler counterexample: source gate, failure class, spurious/genuine classification, deduplication key, pruning effect.
Per-candidate validation matrix result: all gates executed with pass/hold/fail/skipped status, durations, evidence hashes, and aggregate counts.
One permutation corpus row: aggregated statistics for a single candidate across its validation run, used for cross-run pattern analysis.
Aggregate pattern report for one compiler run: successful/failed schema and template patterns, counterexample clusters, contract ambiguity findings, refinement recommendations.

compiler_flow.description: The compiler is a bounded, worktree-isolated, evidence-preserving contract-satisfaction loop. It borrows CEGIS's generator/verifier/counterexample loop and CEGAR's abstraction/refinement/spurious-vs-genuine distinction but does not claim formal verification.
compiler_flow.artifact_flow: run_manifest → candidates.jsonl → validation_results.jsonl → counterexamples.jsonl → permutation_corpus.jsonl → pattern_report → future refinement proposals
compiler_flow.evidence_paths: .build/rig-relay/contract-compiler/runs/<run_id>/{run_manifest.v1.json, candidates.jsonl, validation_results.jsonl, counterexamples.jsonl, permutation_corpus.jsonl, pattern_report.v1.json, worktree_lifecycle.jsonl}

worktree_lifecycle_summary.state_machine: created → patch_applied → validation_running → failed_reset → failed_reaped (OR partially_satisfied → promoted_to_stage → next_slice_search OR fully_satisfied → accepted → promotion_proposal_emitted → cleaned)
worktree_kinds: stage_promotion (longer-lived, carries partial contract satisfaction forward)
accepted_candidate (read-only after acceptance, retained for human review)
worktree_lifecycle_summary.cleanup_policy: Failed scratch worktrees reaped immediately after evidence copied. Quarantined only for novel failures. Stage worktrees retain active lineage + 2 previous. Accepted retained until human checkpoint. Orphans pruned on startup.

counterexample_summary.shape: counterexample_id + source_gate + input_artifact_hash + expected_behavior + actual_behavior_hash + failure_class + spurious_or_genuine + replay_command_hash + deduplication_key + pruning_effect
counterexample_summary.classification: unknown → spurious (caused by imprecise validator/schema/test) or genuine (real contract violation). Classification occurs after replay analysis.
counterexample_summary.pruning: single_candidate, candidate_family, template_branch, schema_constraint_pattern, validator_refinement, contract_refinement, or none.

validation_matrix_summary.outcomes: pass (gate succeeded), hold (non-fatal warning), fail (gate rejected candidate), skipped (gate not run for this candidate)

content_light_posture: All seven schemas enforce content_light: true and redaction_status: content_light. No schema permits raw_prompt, raw_completion, raw_file_contents, raw_credentials, access_token, client_secret, private_repo_contents, or raw absolute paths. Worktree paths are stored as SHA-256 hashes. Artifact bodies are hashed by default. Content-derived data carries SHA-256 prefixes.
non_goals: Generate Python from schemas (no Jinja2 templates created)
Mutate coordination ledger (no coordination events emitted)
Add dependencies (no new packages in pyproject.toml)
Touch GitHub provider, GitHub Actions, release gate validator, CI evidence, OTel dataset
Touch frontend/bridge/backend, MCP, ACP, SDK, A2A
next_recommended_slice: Implement Compiler Experiment 0: generate one Pydantic model for one existing coordination event payload schema, apply in one scratch worktree, validate against the 12 required gates, emit candidate/validation/counterexample evidence using these schemas. Do not implement multi-slice promotion, pattern aggregation, or Jinja2 template infrastructure until Experiment 0 succeeds.
